data.narrative:
Neura Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Reger, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 9 private firms and 1 public company (277810.KQ). Three same-stage, same-sector peers—Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B)—anchor the peer set.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the company's $1.4B total raised as a proxy base, applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to next stage, yielding $2.4B. The peer-median method derives $1.0B from the three comparable firms, with valuations ranging $1.0B–$1.6B. These approaches triangulate to a median implied valuation of $1.7B, with a range of $850M (low) to $2.7B (high).

The $850M–$2.7B range reflects material tension between the stage-progression upside ($2.4B) and peer benchmarks anchored at the median ($1.0B). Key uncertainties include whether the $1.4B raised proxy appropriately reflects current-round value creation, and whether the three-peer sample adequately represents Neura's competitive positioning within the broader robotics ecosystem. The $1.7B median balances both frameworks but warrants stress-testing against revenue, growth rate, and capital efficiency relative to peers.
